title: Snapshot
body:
## What the company is

Sivers Semiconductors AB (ticker: SIVE.ST; OTC US: SIVEF) is a Swedish holding company with two operating subsidiaries that share almost nothing except a parent. **Sivers Wireless AB** makes millimeter-wave beamformers and antenna modules for SATCOM, 5G/6G, and defense applications, claiming to be the only EU-based commercial provider in several beamformer categories; named customers include the European Space Agency and Intelsat. **Sivers Photonics Ltd.** — the UK subsidiary acquired in 2017 as CST Global — designs custom high-power indium-phosphide distributed-feedback lasers and laser arrays, and it is increasingly positioned as the upstream chokepoint for the External Light Source modules that enable co-packaged optics in next-generation AI data-center GPUs. The two businesses share a balance sheet, a Nasdaq Stockholm listing, and an ambition to dual-list in New York. Everything else — technology, geography, customer base — diverges.

At SEK 72.90 × 311.33 million shares outstanding, the market capitalisation sits at approximately SEK 22.7 billion, or roughly $2.2 billion at current exchange rates. That figure warrants an immediate caveat: analyst writeups circulating in early 2025 cited a market cap of around SEK 3.4 billion — a number that, at the time, may have been accurate but has since been rendered obsolete by a rally that accelerated through the CPO narrative. Readers relying on older secondary sources should reset their mental model accordingly.

## Seventy-five years, three acts

The company was founded in 1951 by engineer Carl von Sivers as Sivers Lab AB, manufacturing passive microwave products and slotted-line VSWR detectors for professional and educational markets. Philips Sweden acquired it in 1960. The entity eventually re-emerged as an independent Stockholm-listed company — Sivers IMA Holding AB — before the two acquisitions that created the modern entity: CST Global in 2017 (the Scottish III-V photonics specialist that became Sivers Photonics) and MixComm in 2022 (a US-based millimeter-wave startup that reinforced the wireless segment). The group rebranded as Sivers Semiconductors AB around the same period. What began as a passive-microwave shop for university labs is now marketing itself to the hyperscalers building out AI compute fabric.

## The management team that matters for the US listing

The 2024 CEO transition is the most readable signal of strategic intent. Vickram Vathulya — PhD from Lehigh, MBA from Berkeley Haas, 25 years across NXP, Maxim, and Nuvotronics — was appointed President and CEO on August 19, 2024, with a personal commitment to purchase up to two million shares at a cost of up to $1 million. The commitment is notable for a company at this stage: public skin in the game by an executive whose remit is explicitly to ready Sivers for a US dual listing. Flanking him is Executive Chairman Bami Bastani, a 42-year semiconductor veteran who has run three public-company turnarounds as CEO and served as an SVP at GlobalFoundries. Bastani joined as Strategic Advisor in August 2023 and moved to Executive Chairman in February 2024. The US-listing architecture is the throughline connecting both appointments.

## FY2025: growth, but deeper losses after accounting restatement

The full-year 2025 results, published in the Annual Report on May 13, 2026, carried an unusual asterisk: they had been restated under PCAOB-aligned standards as preparation for the potential US dual listing.

| Metric | Swedish K3 (original) | PCAOB-restated |
|---|---|---|
| Net sales (SEK M) | 304.1 | 306.6 |
| EBIT (SEK M) | −141.3 | −177.8 |
| Net loss (SEK M) | −186.5 | −222.6 |
| EPS (SEK) | −0.69 | −0.81 |
| Equity per share (SEK) | 3.46 | 3.05 |

Revenue grew 25% year-on-year — 33% at constant currency — to SEK 306.6 million. The sales pipeline expanded 64% to $453 million. Free cash outflow narrowed to SEK 66 million from SEK 151 million in 2022, the improvement that the bull case points to as evidence of operating leverage arriving. Cash at year-end was SEK 43.5 million — thin — topped up by a $17 million term loan and convertible debt in February 2026, and then by a non-dilutive $6.6 million Microelectronics Commons Year 2 grant announced on May 19 for US defense infrastructure work. The restatement widened the operating loss by SEK 36 million through revenue reallocations between periods, inventory revaluations, updated share-based compensation assumptions, and impairment of previously capitalised development expenditure. The accounting revision is operationally neutral, but it reveals that prior-period results were reported under standards more forgiving than what a US listing demands. One Substack analyst who had modeled a bull-case fair value of SEK 14.52 per share — implying the current SEK 72.90 is already more than five times their top scenario — noted at the time that the equity story required a very precise sequencing of customer ramps and margin expansion to justify even that figure.

## The question the rest of this report answers

Is Sivers the next LITE — the chokepoint pattern repeating, where a small western laser maker becomes structurally indispensable as hyperscalers standardize on co-packaged optics — or is the at-the-peak valuation pricing a CPO volume ramp that has not yet shipped a single production module? The June 15, 2026 AGM, where shareholders vote on a 15% dilution authority and a board reshuffle that clears out co-founder Fällström, is the first concrete test of whether management can deliver on the architecture they have been promising since 2024.
